title: After-image effect prevents diagonal character movement
description:
With the haste/slow after-image effects active, characters cannot move diagonally in the lobby. They are restricted to moving either:
- Straight up/down (vertical only)
- Forward/backward (horizontal only)

Without haste/slow effects, diagonal movement works normally.

Expected: After-image effect should not interfere with movement controls
Actual: After-images seem to be locking movement to cardinal directions only

This is a regression - likely the after-image rendering or position tracking logic is interfering with the movement input handling.

Affected files:
- client/src/components/game/Lobby.tsx (after-image logic, movement handling)
- Possibly PlayerController movement input code

Related issues:
- ScrumQuest-9o3 (after-image vertical tracking)

Priority: This significantly impacts lobby UX when using haste/slow

title: After-image effect doesn't track vertical position when fly combined with haste/slow
description:

Expected: After-images should trail behind player in both x and y dimensions
Actual: After-images only follow x position, stay at same y level

Affected files:
- client/src/components/game/Lobby.tsx (after-image rendering logic)
- Likely around haste/slow effect state management

Related: Phase 21 (Lobby Magic) - implemented ad-hoc, needs formal polish

title: Design and implement PhaseCoordinator
description:
Create lightweight PhaseCoordinator for hybrid architecture:

ARCHITECTURE (Option C - Hybrid):
- Domains emit events when actions complete
- PhaseCoordinator listens and manages phase transitions
- GameFlowManager orchestrates cross-domain operations

RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Listen to domain events (combat:all_downed, estimation:all_voted, etc)
- Execute phase transitions with validation
- Emit phase_changed events
- Track phase history/state

DESIGN DECISIONS:
- Event contracts for phase triggers
- Validation rules for transitions
- How domains request phase changes

Part of gameState migration (ScrumQuest-ayk parent task).
High complexity - architectural foundation.
